blockers.finding: Lemmas C.1/C.2 are statements about Ringmaster iterates under any computation model (L890, L1234, L1244), but nodes C1 and C2 have no arrival-order or delay-pattern binder: C1/xk and C2/xk depend_on only [d,n,g,x0,gamma,R]. Hence E45/E46 (C1/C2 -> T41, whose execution depends on T41/arr) and E47/E48 (C1/C2 -> DREC, whose recursion is indexed by an arbitrary map a) cannot bind the execution the provider talks about. Related dependency omissions: T41/xk omits arr and gammaT; T51/xk omits v, RT, gammaT; ALG5/xk and L51/xk omit the schedule. In addition E54/E56 bind T41/arr and DEXEC/arr (infinite sequences i_0, i_1, ...) to 'the arrival order induced by the universal computation model', which can be finite when the workers' total work is finite; DEXEC claims to report 'the time of the K-th update' although its only schedule parameter is arr (no v, so no clock).
blockers.repair: Give C1 and C2 an explicit schedule parameter: either the arrival order arr (with MODA as inherited setup) or, preferably for reuse by DREC, an abstract index map a with k-R < a_k <= k (C2) / a_k <= k (C1) together with the i.i.d. stream, and state the Algorithm-5 instance through DEXEC. Bind it on every edge: E45/E46 a := k - delta^k of the T41/arr execution (or arr := T41/arr); E47/E48 a := DREC/a. Add the schedule (arr or v) and gammaT/RT to the depends_on lists of the iterate objects (C1/xk, C2/xk, T41/xk, T51/xk, ALG5/xk, L51/xk). For E54/E55/E56 define the bound sequence as the first R*Kbar MODU arrivals (which exist by DDEAD when T_Kbar < infinity) followed by an arbitrary continuation, and record in T51 or DEXEC that x^0..x^{R Kbar} depend only on i_0..i_{R Kbar - 1}. Either add v (and the MODU clock) as a DEXEC parameter for the universal-model case, or split DEXEC into an arrival-order correspondence plus a MODU schedule lemma that supplies the arrival order and update times.

blockers.finding: E57 binds L51's T0 to 'T_j (start of each block ...)'. L51/start requires that an iteration start exactly at time T0; T_j is only an upper bound on the time of update jR (source L1429: iteration R+1 starts 'before time T_1'). The source then uses T(R, s) <= T(R, T_1) for s <= T_1 (L1430-1432), i.e. monotonicity of T(R, .) in its start time, which is neither recorded in DDEAD nor in the edge.
blockers.repair: Bind T0 := s_{jR}, the time at which update jR is performed (iteration jR+1 starts), with uses of the DDEAD induction hypothesis s_{jR} <= T_j; add to DDEAD (as a stated step or clause) that T(R, s) <= T(R, T_j) = T_{j+1} for s <= T_j because v_i >= 0, which also discharges L51/finite whenever T_{j+1} < infinity.

L151: each worker computes independent unbiased stochastic gradients. Clause: samples used by distinct computed gradients are independent draws from D. L890: Theorem 4.1 is valid under any computation model. In Algorithm 5 the iterates depend on computation times only through which worker's gradient is applied at each update (i, L582); with times not depending on samples (deterministic or conditioned on, L881) every arrival sequence is realizable (stops keep each applied delay <= R-1). Encoding 'any computation model' as an arbitrary deterministic, sample-independent arrival sequence (i_k) is therefore faithful and covers the universal model as an instance.
